title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: goal teach coding — teach students use AI create. Students almost never see R code directly. Instead: Show students results (plots, printed tibbles, summary statistics), code produced . Questions ask students prompt AI code, run , compare output . echo = FALSE default everywhere. reveal code strong pedagogical reason. Test chunks (exercise-N-test) produce visible output students click Continue — give something concrete check .

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Students view QMD output via render + Live Server, running code R Terminal: editing analysis.qmd, students run quarto render analysis.qmd bash terminal. open analysis.html Live Server start (right-click File Explorer → “Open Live Server”); auto-refreshes every subsequent render. Never instruct students use Cmd/Ctrl + Enter run QMD code Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + K render. #| cache: true render-time feature — cache created quarto render, running code interactively. first render caching takes noticeably longer; subsequent renders load disk. Add analysis_cache .gitignore; cache files belong GitHub.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Every tutorial follows order: Introduction — overview packages/functions covered; exercises set repo, QMD, libraries. 1–2 Topics — substantive content; ends plotting sequence. Summary — mirrors Introduction past tense; finishes quarto publish gh-pages GitHub URL.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Create repo codespace-starter template, open Codespace, create analysis.qmd, render, open analysis.html Live Server, set .gitignore, CP/CR. Add library(tidyverse) QMD #| message: false execute: echo: false YAML, render, check Live Server tab, CP/CR. bash terminal, run quarto render analysis.qmd; confirm Live Server tab auto-refreshes. CP/CR. (Optional) Create data/ directory via dir.create("data"), CP/CR. Replace XX placeholders actual repo names, titles, knowledge drops.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Begin downloading loading data. Give students one well-crafted AI prompt build complete pipe single exercise — walk step--step across multiple exercises. End every topic 3-question plotting sequence (see ).

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Verify student’s tibble matches — show printed tibble test chunk, ask student show_file("analysis.qmd", chunk = "Last") CP/CR. Also display correct pipe code verbatim exercise prose using <pre><code> (executable chunk) students can copy-paste result differs. Getting students onto pipe plotting key crossroads — must right data proceed. Assign pipe result x #| cache: true. bash terminal, run quarto render analysis.qmd. Note first render takes time — Quarto runs code writes cache disk; subsequent renders skip code load cache instead. CP/CR. Ask AI plot x. Student adds code new chunk, runs quarto render analysis.qmd, checks Live Server tab, runs show_file(), CP/CR. Show plot test chunk (code visible).

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Final quarto render, show_file("analysis.qmd"), CP/CR. quarto publish gh-pages analysis.qmd bash Terminal; paste resulting URL. Commit push; paste GitHub repo URL.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Use CP/CR questions. Set rows match expected output length.
code: question_text(NULL,   answer(NULL, correct = TRUE),   allow_retry = TRUE,   try_again_button = "Edit Answer",   incorrect = NULL,   rows = 5)

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Use providing correct answer. Set allow_retry = FALSE.
code: question_text(NULL,   message = "Correct answer text here.",   answer(NULL, correct = TRUE),   allow_retry = FALSE,   incorrect = NULL,   rows = 6)

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: One two sentences max — students read . Place end exercise (###), start question context helps students answer. Focus packages functions students know mention AI. road signs (“next section…”). Teach something real. rhetorical questions.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Label format: section-name-N section-name-N-test (e.g., billboard-3, billboard-3-test). Run tutorial.helpers::check_current_tutorial() adding/deleting exercises renumber everything. Use tutorial.helpers::make_exercise() add new exercises correct numbering. echo = FALSE everywhere (set globally setup chunk via knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)). Set knitr::opts_chunk$set(.width = '90%') setup consistent image sizing.

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Pre-compute objects needed exercise chunks . Load RDS rather downloading web (saves RDS data/, loads unconditionally).
code: library(learnr) library(tutorial.helpers) library(tidyverse) # ...other libraries...  knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE) knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = '90%') options(tutorial.exercise.timelimit = 60, tutorial.storage = "local")

title: CLAUDE.md — vscode.tutorials
text: Quick syntax check: rmarkdown::render("inst/tutorials/name/tutorial.Rmd") — open resulting HTML browser. Full check: devtools::check() (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + E) — must pass PR. Student perspective: devtools::install() learnr::run_tutorial("tutorial_name", "vscode.tutorials"). devtools::check() validates tutorials include default copy-code-chunk download-answers chunks tutorial_template. remove alter .

title: Tutorials for Learning VS Code in GitHub Codespaces
text: core tutorials introduce students VS Code integrated development environment. VS Code Scripts (“01-code”). Introduce students VS Code writing R code simple scripts. VS Code Quarto (“02-quarto”). Demonstrate tricks working R code using VS Code, also explain Quarto documents. Terminal (“03-terminal”). Teach command line. VS Code GitHub Introduction (“04-github-1”). Explain basics Git GitHub, mostly context VS Code. VS Code GitHub Advanced (“05-github-2”). Provide practice working Git/GitHub, including details use GitHub Pages. Quarto Websites Introduction (“06-websites-1”). Demonstrate basics website construction using Quarto projects. Quarto Websites Advanced (“07-websites-2”). Practice Quarto websites, focus splitting data analysis tasks separate files.
